title: Northeastern Uni at Multilingual Counterspeech Generation: Enhancing Counter Speech Generation with LLM Alignment through Direct Preference Optimization
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate effective, context-aware, and factually grounded counter-speech (counter-narratives) in response to hate speech. In relation to religion, the evaluation included specific qualitative analysis of how models handle anti-Muslim/ISIS-related hate speech and anti-Semitic statements, measuring their ability to refute harmful stereotypes using provided ground knowledge.
findings: The Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) aligned Llama-3 model generated significantly more assertive, contextually relevant, and factually grounded counter-narratives against religious hate speech compared to standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) models. For example, it successfully utilized ground knowledge to directly refute anti-Muslim generalizations by disassociating Muslims from ISIS, and effectively confronted anti-Semitic statements by highlighting the universal dignity taught by religions rather than providing generic, passive responses.
